items.title: Shanghai invasive-BCI startup Active Technology (主动科技) raises RMB 464M Angel+ round, bringing total angel funding to about RMB 800M
items.summary: Active Technology, founded in February 2026, closed a RMB 464 million Angel+ round led by Gaorong Ventures, SDIC Pilot Fund and Shanghai Technology Venture Capital, with existing investors including DT Capital and BGI Songhe following on. items.title: Stanford launches Digital Brain Project to build open brain foundation models from 7T MRI and wearable OPM-MEG data
items.summary: Stanford's Wu Tsai Neurosciences Institute launched a five-year Digital Brain Project, with lead philanthropic support from Mark and Mary Stevens and Clara Wu Tsai, to collect large-scale human brain data using 7T MRI and wearable OPM-MEG and use it to train brain foundation models. Stanford says the data and models will be openly shared through standards such as BIDS/OpenNeuro.

details.hub_relevance: Open, large-scale brain foundation models and datasets built with wearable OPM-MEG could become reference resources and benchmarks for Hub neural-data analysis and AI tooling work.
details.review_notes: Institutional initiative/philanthropic launch, not a paper. Also covered by Inside BCI on 2026-11-04.

items.summary: Neurotronics, a Nihon Kohden company, announced FDA 510(k) clearance (K261521, cleared October 9, 2026) for its Sleep Analysis Module, an AI/ML software tool that estimates total sleep time from PPG/pulse-oximetry signals for home sleep apnea testing. items.title: Standard touchscreen test procedures shift circadian rhythms in mice: a modified protocol to minimize circadian confounds
items.summary: Continuous home-cage circadian activity monitoring of mice undergoing daily operant/touchscreen testing, with control of chamber and home-cage lighting (stated method); authors state individual activity records were not available for pair-housed females because overhead PIR sensors give a cage-level aggregate (stated limitation).

details.facts: Stated (full text, bioRxiv preprint, CC BY-NC 4.0): Bussey-Saksida touchscreen chambers (Campden/Lafayette ABET II, Whisker); home-cage locomotor activity by overhead passive-infrared sensors with ClockLab (Actimetrics); standard screen light (~21 lux) caused ~3.5 h phase delay after 7 days of early-dark testing; 10 lighting conditions tested; recommendations include treating the chamber as a light source, brighter home-cage lighting, removing short-wavelength light, periodic DD probes. Limitations stated: pair-housed females lacked individual activity records (aggregate could mask one mouse shifting); bright home-cage light levels difficult to standardize.
details.inferences: Per-animal wearable movement plus proximity logging (Juxta) could give individual activity rhythms in pair-housed mice; Hub Wheel with Hublink logs wheel turns and in-cage light, which could document home-cage lux alongside rhythms; FED3/FED4 home-cage operant testing could be a low-light alternative to moving mice to touchscreen chambers (collaboration, not sales). Equivalence of these devices to PIR/ClockLab phase estimates is untested. No purchasing intent stated; lab already has PIR/ClockLab.
details.product_matches_raw: Juxta Social Proximity Loggers (Gen5); Hub Wheel with Hublink; Body Event Analysis Module 3 (BEAM3); FED3 (Feeding Experimentation Device 3); FED4 (Feeding Experimentation Device 4)
details.recommended_action: Human review; strong methods fit for circadian/operant segment (individual rhythms in pair housing, in-cage light logging, home-cage operant alternative via FED3/FED4). No outreach from Scout.
details.review_note: Preprint (not peer reviewed); open-license full text read for methods. Not in Outreach Log; no existing-relationship overlap. Key investigator not in Atlas; REQ-OPP-OPP-060 filed 2026-11-04. Co-author Ralph Mistlberger (SFU) is a senior circadian PI, not listed as key.

items.title: Voluntary exercise mitigates the effects of peri-adolescent social isolation on emotion recognition and the oxytocinergic system in male mice
items.summary: Chronic (12-week) home-cage voluntary wheel running in singly- vs group-housed mice, with running distance quantified across housing conditions (stated method).

details.facts: Stated (full text, Journal of Neuroendocrinology, CC BY-NC-ND, read via Europe PMC PMC13716504): weaned male C57BL/6J mice singly- or group-housed with an igloo or a Bio-Serv fast-track running wheel (Bioseb, France) for 12 weeks; wheel use checked as mean daily rotations per cage divided by mice per cage, collected at least 3 days/week over 4 weeks, converted to distance; individual running evaluated only in a 10-min test after 24 h deprivation. Isolation enhanced social investigation and impaired emotion discrimination and reduced PVN oxytocin neurons; exercise protected emotion discrimination and raised plasma OXT.
details.inferences: Continuous, wireless per-wheel logging (Hub Wheel with Hublink) could replace intermittent per-cage counts in this kind of chronic exercise x housing design; Juxta could add individual social-contact data in group-housed cages. Inference only: authors state no equipment gap or purchasing intent, and the lab already uses commercial wheels.

items.title: Scheduled, logged, weatherproof playback for unattended field playback experiments
items.summary: Playback experiments are a core field-ecology method, but requiring a human present disrupts behavior and limits sample size (BoomBox, Methods Ecol Evol). The leading open option, BoomBox (~$75), is trigger-only with ~15 min of MP3 audio. ACORN adds scheduled/random daily programs, IP65 housing, ~103 dB output, and CSV environment logs. The gap is partly validated (need is documented); demand at ACORN's $799 price is a hypothesis.

items.title: Wireless fleet data retrieval for the FED3 installed base
items.summary: FED3 logs to an on-board microSD card, so labs running many cages collect data by hand. The Hub's own Nov 2024 post estimates 100+ labs and 3,000+ FED3 devices. On FEDforum, users have built one-off Wi-Fi workarounds, and FED's developer called multi-device wireless harvesting 'not trivial'. Users also report university IT network restrictions that block ESP32 Wi-Fi devices. Hublink's BLE gateway sidesteps campus Wi-Fi, already has a FED3 integration path (ESP32-S3 Feather + SD backpack + multi-architecture FED3 library), and FED4 v1.7 lists optional Hublink BLE sync. Need is documented; willingness to pay for a retrofit or subscription is untested.

items.title: Cage-scale programmable spatial foraging compatible with chronic neural recording
items.summary: Open naturalistic-foraging platforms are either room-scale or head-fixed. SWC's Aeon habitat is about 2.7 x 2.4 m with wheel-based foraging patches. Dynamic-foraging tasks such as Allen's are rig-based. FED3 offers single-location operant feeding in the home cage. No widely adopted tool appears to turn a standard home-cage floor into a distributed, programmable reward and cue field that works with chronic recordings, which is SFP's design. This is a hypothesis from a desk scan, not a validated gap: no user survey or demand data yet, and SFP is alpha stage and not for sale.
